about: Born, Not Made, simplified version after the sketch of 21 November 2026. Frame: x toward the opening, y port, z up, meters; origin on the docking plane, on the inner floor (the tank floor is 3 mm lower).

stages.name: Dock
stages.text: The tail docks to the gel chamber from above: the rack of the tail reaches over the bowl, and three disc magnets close the thin docking ring.

stages.name: Unfold, gel
stages.text: The arm unfolds and injects the gel: 3.1 L at 0.1 L per minute. This is the first fill; the gel then stays in the bowl from birth to birth. Then the water comes in.

stages.name: Kit
stages.text: The electromagnet picks the electronics kit once, from the store in the tail, and places the kit in the gel, before any printing.

stages.name: Tool change
stages.text: One tool change at the rack in the tail: holder off, print needle on (Rotrics quick release).

stages.name: Print
stages.text: The DexArm prints the folded newborn around the kit: 44 m of bead, 0.08 L of Dragon Skin 10 NV.

stages.name: Cure, change
stages.text: Cure, and the second tool change: print needle off, holder on.

stages.name: Air in, nose up
stages.text: The ball needle enters the valve. Air pushes the trapped gel out of the folds, the newborn floats up in the gel, and the arm presses the tail end down so the nose rises above the lip.

stages.name: Push while inflating
stages.text: The arm steers the tail end from above and pushes; the newborn slides over the lip, and each segment opens outside. No contractions.

stages.name: Hold and fill
stages.text: The arm holds, the newborn fills to full size, the needle lets go.

stages.name: Float
stages.text: The newborn floats in the water: gravity, buoyancy, drag, a damped settling.

stages.name: Swim
stages.text: The newborn takes ballast, sits lower and swims on two jets.

notes: The tail is lowered onto the tank floor behind the gel chamber; the tools on the rack and the kit in the cradle go down into the wells and the neck of the bowl. Three magnets close the dry seam.
The arm unfolds out of the tail, between the two parked modules, over the gel bowl. The base does not move.
Gel comes through the line on the arm; the arm moves the outlet over three fill points.
With the gel in, the tank is filled with water to 93 mm. The gel stands higher than the water at the seam.
The bare arm folds back between the two parked modules in the tail.
The bare arm turns in behind the holder: an electromagnet and a ball needle.
The quick release slides onto the holder and clicks.
The holder slides forward out of the fork.
The holder moves along the narrow well to the kit store, in the neck on the centerline of the tail.
The needle goes down into the well of the kit; the magnet lands on the steel disk.
Magnet on: the magnet holds the kit by the steel disk.
The kit is carried forward through the gel and up, out of the tail, over the print seat.
The kit goes straight down through the gel onto the three seat bumps.
Magnet off: the kit stays on the seat, held by the gel; the holder lifts clear.
Tool change in the tail: the holder goes back through the neck.
The holder goes back into the fork, along the narrow well.
The pin on the fork presses the release; the module stays.
The bare arm turns 48 degrees, behind the modules, to the print needle.
The quick release clicks onto the print needle.
The needle slides forward out of the fork, through the gel.
The needle goes forward through the gel to the kit.
The folded newborn is printed around the kit, layer by layer, in clear silicone.
The silicone cures in the gel (75 minutes at room temperature). The print needle goes back to the rack in the tail.
The holder is back on the arm: the ball needle beside the magnet now carries the air.
The ball needle goes to the valve on the tail end of the newborn.
Air at 450 Pa pushes the gel out of the folds through the vent in the nose; the drained newborn rises 29 mm and floats in the gel.
The needle presses the tail end down in the gel: the nose rises above the lip of the opening.
Push while inflating: every segment opens once the segment is out of the opening. All the air comes through the ball needle on the arm.
At full reach the arm holds the needle in the valve while the rest of the air goes in; the skin stretches by a quarter and the creases pull smooth.
The needle lets go. The newborn floats free, rocks and settles; the arm parks the module and folds back into the tail.
The kit pumps take water into the belly pocket until the jets are under water; the newborn swims a slow turn on two jets.

checks.name: Tail shell prints in one piece on the H2S, lying or standing on the docking face: 337 x 314 x 336 mm of 340 x 320 x 340

Rack frame of the tail (forks, cradle, beams) is a small print of its own, 81 x 318 x 98 mm, that slides into two dovetail sockets on the tail wall: with the rack printed on, the tail would be 392 mm long, and no tilt of the print brings that under 340 mm
Head prints in two pieces: the head 269 x 314 x 336 mm and the snout 100 x 186 x 246 mm, bonded and sealed at the root of the snout (head and snout in one piece would be 366 mm long)
Folded arm ends 6 mm behind the docking plane; tower top 11 mm under the tail roof
Rack and kit cradle are one frame of the tail: they reach 55 mm forward of the docking plane, over the bowl of the head, with the forks 4 mm above the gel; the head carries no rack and no shelf
The print needle reaches all 1440 sampled print points inside the official joint ranges

The parts dock and take the gel in the dry tank. With the gel in and 93 mm of water, the tail weighs 5.5 kg against 5.1 kg of buoyancy (with the 5 mm steel plate under the arm base and 0.21 kg of extra steel)
The filled gel chamber rests on the floor: weight 4.7 kg, buoyancy 3.9 kg
Without gel the parts would lift in the water (together 7.3 kg against 8.9 kg of buoyancy), so the gel goes in before the water, and the bowl is not emptied under water

The lip of the mouth is 17 mm above the water and 3 mm above the gel. The docking seam is dry: the whole bowl, with the neck and the two wells, is in the head print, and the rear wall of the neck stands 4 mm ahead of the docking plane
The gel stays in the bowl between births: 3.12 L in the bowl, about 19 mL leave with each newborn (0.6 percent); the level falls 0.6 mm a birth, topped up through the arm
The lip is 3 mm above the gel surface; the yield stress of the gel holds a crest of about 2.5 mm, and the folded print has already raised the level before the push

All parts lie in line inside the taper, behind a printed bulkhead 72 mm behind the arm axis: first the two silicone bores with their stepper and the inflator, then the battery with the gel pump, the controller board nearest the tip; the nearest a part comes to the shell is 5.5 mm
Energy for one cycle about 25 Wh (the Raspberry Pi 5 takes a third); the battery (six 18650 cells) holds 54 Wh: margin 2.1. The inflator runs on a battery of its own
Silicone: the two bores hold 119 mL, one newborn takes 83 mL

Air: the inflator of the artist fills a size 7 basketball (7.6 L, 55 kPa) in 35 s, which is 7.1 L of free air per minute; the newborn (11.2 L at 1.3 kPa) fills in about 95 s. The inflator must stop at 1.3 kPa: the preset of a tire inflator may not go that low (open question)
Every pose of the timeline is inside the official joint ranges (base -24 to 24, J1 0 to 55, J2 2 to 85 degrees)

Electromagnet (Adafruit 3872, 2.5 kg holding force): lifting force taken as a tenth, 2.5 N, through the thin silicone over the steel disk; the kit weighs 1.08 N in air and about 0.00 N in the gel: margin 2.3

Release in the gel: with the magnet off, the yield stress of the gel holds the seated kit with about 0.19 N; a remanent pull of 2 percent would be 0.05 N (estimate; a short reverse pulse makes the release certain)
The steel disk adds 2.5 g on top of the kit; the metacentric height with ballast stays 62 mm
Payload while carrying the kit: 193 g of 500 g
Force of the needle on the valve stays under the payload: peak 3.97 N of 4.91 N
The rubber ball valve grips the needle against the largest upward pull: 1.38 N of about 2 N (estimate, to bench test)
The newborn leaves through the center of the opening: in the middle of the push the axis of the body crosses the face 20 mm from the center of the 160 x 172 mm opening
Folds can be printed: story pitch 3.6 mm with one valley, pleat walls 7.1 mm apart at mid depth (limit: 1.2 mm wall plus 2 mm of gel)
Kresling stories are bistable with a barrier strain of 2.2 percent, far under the 25 percent stretch of the skin
Stretch 1.25 stays under the limit point of the membrane (1.38) and uses 4 percent of the 663 percent elongation at break
Full size 428 x 301 mm against the gel chamber 366 x 314 x 336 mm: 117 percent of the length, 96 percent of the width
The newborn floats upright: metacentric height 39 mm dry, 62 mm with ballast
Draft 38 mm dry; 0.14 kg of water in the belly pocket puts the jets 45 mm under water
The motion settles: pitch rate in the last three seconds under 0.03 degrees per second; deepest contact at the lip 0.12 mm
Per frame penetration test over 2400 frames: deepest overlap of any pair 0.78 mm (limit 1 mm)
UNS 150U: the parent body (703 mm long, 336 mm tall) and the newborn (428 mm) in the 1470 mm inner length, with a swim run of 639 mm; water 69 L, about 203 kg filled

deriv.name: Arm base
deriv.value: fixed, 103 mm behind the docking plane, on a 5 mm steel plate on the tail floor
deriv.why: The folded DexArm reaches 97 mm ahead of its axis. Ahead of the folded arm the tail needs 6 mm more for the rack: the modules hang 150 mm ahead of the axis, the nearest the arm can hold a tool. From there the tool tip reaches 393 mm from the axis at the height of the print.

deriv.name: Tail
deriv.value: 334 mm long from the docking plane to the tip, 17.8 L; shell print 337 x 314 x 336 mm
deriv.why: One long convex taper to a small tip, in side view and in plan. The sides start to close 18 mm behind the docking plane, right behind the ring with the magnets: the arm works only 24 degrees to each side, so the tail needs its full width nowhere but at the ring (the turntable is 184 mm wide, the tail is 259 mm wide there). The roof falls from 20 mm behind the arm axis, where the tower ends (the folded arm is 314 mm tall); the floor rises from 70 mm behind the axis, where the base plate ends. All three run on ogive curves (exponents 1.25 to 1.3; an ellipse has 2) to one tip 120 mm above the floor, 231 mm behind the arm axis. The section turns from a flat bottomed arch at the ring to an ellipse at the tip. Over the whole timeline the arm comes no nearer to the shell than 5 mm. Volume 17.8 L (round 5: 19.8 L, round 4: 23.1 L) although the shell is 56 mm longer (334 mm against 278 mm). Print: lying, or standing on the docking face, 3, 6 and 4 mm clear of the H2S. This length is only possible because the rack frame is a print of its own: with the rack printed on, the tail would be 392 mm long, and a search over all tilts in steps of 5 degrees finds no orientation that fits (the first 100 mm behind the ring fill the 314 x 336 mm section). With the rack printed on, the tip could stand no further than 279 mm behind the plane.

deriv.name: Print needle
deriv.why: The head stays above the gel (92 mm deep over the lowest printed point) while the tip prints the lowest layer.

deriv.name: Printed newborn
deriv.why: With the needle hanging 122 mm below the wrist, the arm reaches from 206 mm to 393 mm from its axis at the axis of the print, and from 237 mm to 371 mm at the top of the print. The 150 mm body lies from 221 mm to 371 mm. The 90 mm diameter is the smallest that holds the kit on the belly.

deriv.name: Full size newborn
deriv.why: The skin that packs into the folded volume at the packing of the full size study (silicone 47 percent of the folded volume): 0.170 m2. Kresling stories (n = 16, twist 14.3 degrees a story) open the length, sixteen star pleats open the girth, a 25 percent stretch pulls the creases smooth. Unfolding at about 300 Pa (estimate), full at 1251 Pa.

deriv.name: Shape of the newborn
deriv.value: one smooth spindle, widest at 62 percent of the length
deriv.why: Eight segments between nine rings follow one curve: a blunt tail end of 38 mm radius with the valve, a long taper, the widest ring (151 mm radius), a shorter taper to the nose. Unchanged from round 5. The three slender stories at the tail end (rings up to 78 mm radius) open inside the snout; their lengthening carries the wide rings out past the lip, and each wide segment opens only once outside.

deriv.name: Gel bowl
deriv.value: 3.12 L of gel, flat surface at 104 mm
deriv.why: The bowl lies in the head. Its floor is flat; its front is one straight ramp at 40 degrees, 166 mm long, that starts 332 mm from the arm axis, under the tapered nose of the folded print (with 4 mm of gel under each ring), runs out through the snout and reaches the lip 128 mm further forward. How flat the ramp can be is set by the arm: the ball needle reaches 347 mm from the arm axis at the height of the valve (165 mm), and a flatter ramp puts the lip further away, so a wider ring of the newborn stands in the snout while the last air goes in. Searched with the full size newborn held at full reach, clear by 3 mm and with the force under the payload: 40, 42.5 and 45 degrees pass with an opening of 160 mm or less; 37.5 degrees needs 180 mm, 35 degrees 200 mm, 30 degrees 230 mm. Behind the bowl, up to the docking plane, the head has a terrace at rim height with one neck 68 mm wide for the kit and two narrow wells for the tool stems: 0.59 L of the total.

deriv.name: Docking plane
deriv.value: 103 mm ahead of the arm axis, a thin 4 mm ring, three magnets, dry
deriv.why: The plane stands right ahead of the arm: the folded arm ends 6 mm behind the plane, the base plate 25 mm. The seam is dry and carries no seal: no gel touches the seam, the rear wall of the neck is 4 mm ahead of the plane, and the plane is closed below the rim by the rear wall of the head. This works because the rack and the kit cradle are arms of the tail print that reach forward over the bowl, so the tools hang with their stems in the wells of the head and no tool crosses a wall. The price: the tail docks from above (the stems and the kit go down into the wells and the neck), not by sliding along the floor. Three DC2-N52 disc magnets on steel discs hold 161 N.

deriv.name: Rack and kit store
deriv.value: one frame of the tail, 150 mm ahead of the arm axis, 24 degrees to each side
deriv.why: Close to its base the DexArm holds the wrist at 134 mm and no higher, so a module hangs with the head 112 mm above the floor, the ball needle of the holder at 57 mm and the print needle tip at 12 mm. No wall can stand between such a tool and the print, so the tools hang over the bowl, stems in two narrow wells of the head (gel surface 104 mm). The forks, 4 mm above the gel, the kit cradle and their beams are one flat frame (81 x 318 x 98 mm, a small print) with two dovetail tongues that slide into sockets printed on the tail wall just behind the docking plane. The frame belongs to the tail: the head stays bare. The bare quick release comes up behind a module (33 mm of travel), clicks on, and slides the module forward out of the fork. Rechecked in round 6, hanging the tools beside the arm inside the tail: the print needle tip can be lifted to 18 mm at most there and the ball needle to 63 mm, against a bowl wall of 108 mm, so the stems would have to cross the docking plane in gel filled slots and the seam would be wet. Moving the arm axis closer to the plane would not bring the snout closer either: the print lies where the arm can reach the top layers without leaning back (J1 cannot go below 0), 237 mm from the axis.

deriv.name: Opening
deriv.value: the end of the snout: an ellipse of 160 x 172 mm standing on the lip; lip 466 mm from the arm axis, 107 mm high
deriv.why: The snout sticks out 97 mm in front of the head. The lip continues the line of the gel surface: 3 mm above the gel (the yield stress of the gel holds a crest of about 2.5 mm) and 17 mm above the water. The opening is set by the ring of the newborn that passes the lip while the body is stretched to full size: about 140 mm across at a pitch of 20 degrees. In the middle of the push the axis of the folded body crosses the end of the snout 20 mm from its center. The end face leans back 4 degrees.

deriv.name: Head (gel chamber)
deriv.value: 269 x 314 x 336 mm outside, with a snout of 100 x 186 x 246 mm
deriv.why: The head closes on a round front, 369 mm from the arm axis: 7 mm ahead of the module head when the arm holds the valve at full reach. From that front the snout sticks out 97 mm, a tube of 164 x 180 mm inside. Head and snout together are 366 mm long, more than the H2S prints, so the snout is the third printed piece the artist allowed: the cut stands at the root of the snout, the joint is a 6 mm socket, bonded and sealed (the joint lies below the gel line at the ramp). The head carries the bowl with the neck and the wells, the first 48 mm of the ramp and three seat bumps; the snout carries the rest of the ramp and the lip.

deriv.name: Water
deriv.why: Deep enough for the newborn with ballast (draft 45 mm) with 48 mm under the belly; low enough to stay 17 mm under the lip and 14 mm under the gel.

deriv.name: Time
deriv.why: First gel fill 31 min at 0.1 L per minute (micro peristaltic pump; later cycles only top up), print 43 min for 44 m of bead at 20 mm per second, cure 75 min, air about 95 s for 11.2 L: the inflator adds 55 kPa to a 7.6 L basketball in 35 s, so 7.6 x 55 / 101 = 4.1 L of free air in 35 s, 7.1 L per minute.

deriv.name: Tail contents
deriv.value: 6 parts, 0.75 kg, at the tail end
deriv.why: Cut to what one cycle needs, with the parts of the artist. Air: the CaRSun cordless inflator, 75 x 60 x 32 mm, with a battery of its own. Controller: the Raspberry Pi 5. Battery for the arm, the controller and the small pumps: about 25 Wh a cycle (arm 12 W while moving, estimate), six 18650 cells hold 54 Wh. Gel: one micro peristaltic pump; no gel store, the gel stays in the bowl. Silicone: two bores of the print with pistons, 119 mL for the 83 mL of one newborn. The kit is picked by a 5 V electromagnet (20 mm, 22.7 g) on the holder, switched by the Raspberry Pi 5, on a steel disk on top of the kit: no vacuum system. The newborn carries a ball inflation valve; the ball inflation needle stands beside the magnet on the holder, with the three way stopcock on the arm, set by hand before the cycle. The two FIT0800 water pumps stay in the kit of the newborn. All of these sit at the tail end behind a thin printed bulkhead, inside the taper, on printed seats.

deriv.name: Printing the parts
deriv.value: four prints: tail shell, rack frame, head, snout
deriv.why: Tail shell: 337 x 314 x 336 mm, about 1.2 kg of clear PETG at a 3 mm wall with the bulkhead, about 14 h at 18 mm3 per second; standing on the docking face the taper closes without supports. Rack frame: 81 x 318 x 98 mm, flat. Head: 269 x 314 x 336 mm, about 1.7 kg with the snout, about 21 h, standing on the docking face. Snout: 100 x 186 x 246 mm, standing on its root.

verdict.point: A real snout in front of the head, as a third printed piece
verdict.why: The snout sticks out 97 mm from the round front of the head: a tube of 164 x 180 mm inside, printed on its own (100 x 186 x 246 mm) and bonded on at its root. Head 269 x 314 x 336 mm.

verdict.point: One long ramp at about 30 to 45 degrees, from the bowl floor out through the snout
verdict.why: Straight, 166 mm long, from the bowl floor 332 mm from the arm axis to the lip at the end of the snout. Flatter does not hold with this arm: at 37.5 degrees the opening would have to be 180 mm, at 35 degrees 200 mm, at 30 degrees 230 mm, because the ball needle reaches only 347 mm from the arm axis at the height of the valve.

verdict.point: The tail reads as pointed: a long convex taper to a small tip, in side view and in plan
verdict.why: Sides from 18 mm behind the docking plane, roof from the arm tower, floor from the base plate, on ogive curves to one tip 334 mm behind the plane. 17.8 L (round 5: 19.8 L).

verdict.point: Equipment in line inside the taper, biggest nearest the arm, smallest at the tip
verdict.why: 0.75 kg: the silicone bores with their stepper and the inflator, then the battery (54 Wh) with the gel pump, then the Raspberry Pi 5, between 72 mm and 171 mm behind the arm axis. The last 60 mm to the tip stay empty: no part is that small.

Tail shell 337 x 314 x 336 mm, rack frame 81 x 318 x 98 mm, head 269 x 314 x 336 mm, snout 100 x 186 x 246 mm, against 340 x 320 x 340 mm. The rack frame is separate because the tail with the rack printed on would be 392 mm long in every orientation.

verdict.point: Docking seam at the arm tower, dry
verdict.why: The plane stands 103 mm ahead of the arm axis, 25 mm ahead of the base plate. The seam is dry and has no seal. Three disc magnets, 161 N, on a 4 mm ring. The tail docks from above.

verdict.point: The arm at the very front of the tail, on a fixed base; folds back, unfolds to work
verdict.why: Axis 103 mm behind the docking plane; the folded arm ends 6 mm behind the plane; all 2400 poses of the timeline are inside the joint ranges.

verdict.point: Arm axis closer to the seam, rack beside the arm
verdict.why: Beside the arm the tools hang inside the tail, and their tips (18 mm and 63 mm at most) cannot be lifted over the 108 mm wall of the bowl: the seam would be wet. A shorter distance to the seam would also not move the snout closer to the arm: the place of the print is set by the nearest point the arm reaches without leaning back.

verdict.point: Flat gel surface, about 3 L or less
verdict.why: 3.12 L, surface at 104 mm, of which 0.59 L in the neck and the two wells. The longer ramp adds about 0.2 L to the 2.91 L of round 5.

verdict.point: Tool modules, tool changes and the kit store in the tail, a bare head
verdict.why: The rack frame slides into the tail and reaches 55 mm forward of the docking plane, over the bowl. The head print carries no rack, no shelf and no insert.

verdict.point: The parent body rests on the tank floor; only the newborn floats
verdict.why: In 93 mm of water the tail weighs 5.5 kg (with steel under the arm base) against 5.1 kg of buoyancy, the filled gel chamber 4.7 kg against 3.9 kg.
Printed 150 x 90 mm, full size 428 x 301 mm, 11.2 L, as in round 5: 61 percent of the length of the whole parent body (703 mm with the snout and the longer tail).

verdict.point: Birth by pushing while inflating, all air through the arm
verdict.why: The needle steers the tail end from above and pushes the folded body up the ramp into the snout; the three slender tail stories open inside the snout and carry the wide segments out; peak force 3.97 N of 4.91 N. The valve stays 119 mm short of the lip: the part outside is carried by the water.

limits: Open points on the parts: a tire inflator may not stop as low as 1.3 kPa; the force of the electromagnet through the silicone skin and its release in the gel need a bench test; the product pages of the inflator, the stopcock and the ball valve were read by the artist and the coordinator, not opened from here.

Estimates, to measure: the mass of the DexArm (2.4 kg), the power of the DexArm while moving (12 W), the mass of the inflator, the size of the micro pumps beyond the published figures, the module head (30 x 40 x 52 mm), the seal of the cup, the flow of gel through a 3.5 mm tube, the pressure that opens the folds (300 Pa), the yield stress of the gel (25 Pa), the pump curve of the kit pumps, friction at the lip (0.2).

How the official joint angles J1 and J2 map onto the link meshes is an assumption, as on the full version. The DexArm specification page could not be opened again from here on 21 November 2026; its numbers are those used on the full version.

The valve is a soft boss on the tail cap and the nozzle stays vertical while the body pitches by up to 36 degrees: this needs a bench test. So does the drain of the gel from the folds, and whether a fold packed this tightly prints and opens as drawn.
The force on the valve is a quasi static estimate from slices: weight, buoyancy in the gel and in the water, the lip with friction, yield drag.

The newborn is drawn rigid with one soft droop where the body leaves the opening; a real skin at 300 Pa also wrinkles. In the force estimate the unfolded part outside is limp at that droop: the lip, the hull front and the water carry that part, and the arm steers only the part still inside. Friction at the gel wet lip is taken as 0.2.
The swim is a straight run on both jets and one slow turn; the speed comes from an estimated pump curve.

In the snout the order in which the segments open is scripted: the three slender tail stories first, each wide segment once past the lip. A real skin under one pressure opens everywhere at once and presses on the wall of the snout; whether the body then slips out as drawn needs a bench test.
Overlap is measured from sampled points (4 to 11 mm apart) against exact surfaces, so a figure can be about 1 mm off.

read.birth_text: Quasi static estimate from slices. Peak 3.97 N; the payload of the DexArm is 4.91 N. The needle pushes forward and down; the gel carries the body inside, the lip and the water carry the body outside.
read.tank_text: The tank is the Ultum Nature Systems UNS 150U, a rimless low iron glass tank of 1500 x 600 x 600 mm with 15 mm glass (the longest stock length under 1.8 m; no stock tank is 1.3 m). The parent body, 703 mm long and 336 mm tall, stands on the floor at one end; 93 mm of water (69 L) leave the lip of the opening 17 mm above the water and give the newborn 719 mm of open water ahead. Filled as shown the tank weighs about 203 kg.
